title: Trees
statementMd:
On Bertown's main street $*n*$ trees are growing, the tree number $*i*$ has the height of $*a*_{*i*}$ meters ($1 ≤ *i* ≤ *n*$). By the arrival of the President of Berland these trees were decided to be changed so that their heights formed a beautiful sequence. This means that the heights of trees on ends (the $1$st one and the $*n*$-th one) should be equal to each other, the heights of the $2$-nd and the $(*n* - 1)$-th tree must also be equal to each other, at that the height of the $2$-nd tree should be larger than the height of the first tree by $1$, and so on. In other words, the heights of the trees, standing at equal distance from the edge (of one end of the sequence) must be equal to each other, and with the increasing of the distance from the edge by $1$ the tree height must also increase by $1$. For example, the sequences "`2 3 4 5 5 4 3 2`" and "`1 2 3 2 1`" are beautiful, and '`1 3 3 1`" and "`1 2 3 1`" are not.

Changing the height of a tree is a very expensive operation, using advanced technologies invented by Berland scientists. In one operation you can choose any tree and change its height to any number, either increase or decrease. Note that even after the change the height should remain a positive integer, i. e, it can't be less than or equal to zero. Identify the smallest number of changes of the trees' height needed for the sequence of their heights to become beautiful.

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$) which is the number of trees. The second line contains integers $*a*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{5}$) which are the heights of the trees.

## Output

Print a single number which is the minimal number of trees whose heights will have to be changed for the sequence to become beautiful.
statementZhMd:
<statement>
在贝尔镇的主街上生长着 $*n*$ 棵树，第 $*i*$ 棵树的高度为 $*a*_{*i*}$ 米（$1 ≤ *i* ≤ *n*$）。为了迎接贝尔兰总统，人们决定改变这些树的高度，使它们的高度构成一个美丽的序列。也就是说，两端的树（第 $1$ 棵和第 $*n*$ 棵）的高度应当相等，第 $2$ 棵和第 $(*n* - 1)$ 棵树的高度也应当相等，同时第 $2$ 棵树的高度应比第 $1$ 棵树高 $1$，以此类推。换句话说，距离序列某一端相同距离的树，其高度必须相等；而从端点向内的距离每增加 $1$，树的高度也必须增加 $1$。例如，序列 `2 3 4 5 5 4 3 2` 和 `1 2 3 2 1` 是美丽的，而 `1 3 3 1` 和 `1 2 3 1` 不是。

改变树的高度是一项非常昂贵的操作，需要使用贝尔兰科学家发明的先进技术。一次操作中，你可以选择任意一棵树，将它的高度改变为任意数值，可以增加也可以减少。注意，即使改变之后，树的高度也必须保持为正整数，即不能小于或等于零。请确定使树的高度序列变得美丽所需的最少改变次数。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$），表示树的数量。第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{5}$），表示每棵树的高度。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，表示使树的高度序列变得美丽所需改变的树的最少数量。
</statement>
